speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these hand tremors, and do they occur at rest or only when you are trying to move your hands? Also, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting or balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the progressive nature of the tremor and the specific difficulty with reading suggest a postural or action component. Given the recent memory decline regarding bills, have you noticed any changes in his gait or balance, and does the tremor get better when he is sleeping? Also, has he experienced any loss of smell or stiffness in his limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease

I must clarify that iron deficiency anemia does not present with resting tremors, soft speech, or memory decline; your symptoms are classic for a neurodegenerative condition. Please undergo a neurological examination to assess rigidity and reflexes, and we should request imaging to rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.
